gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-jp: Nippo stands tall, its small letters nearly capital-sized. Wire-cut strokes make it the sharper, more technical voice, while Noto Sans JP, with a very tall x-height and sweeping open curves, handles the quiet sans-serif work underneath.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Contemporary and a bit technical, Nippo lays down strokes with no hairlines and no swells anywhere. Noto Sans Kaithi, a sans-serif with lowercase that fills the line like capitals, sits beside it as a close, easygoing relative.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Nippo's strokes look cut from wire, with no tapering where they meet or end. Noto Sans Kannada brings gentler steps from small letters to capitals and s curves that open wide, so the two feel friendly together.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li reads clean, with brush ends lifted away before each curve closes and capitals barely taller than lowercase. Nippo's single-thickness lines make the pair crisp.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Noto Sans Kharoshthi runs dark through each line, its curves never closing. Nippo is the one for standout lettering with a pen line holding one width, while the body font simply carries the text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer cuts generous openings, like chisel notches in wood, into small letters that stand almost capital-sized. Nippo draws the flat fineliner line.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Marker-plain and wire-cut, Nippo looks modern and a little technical. Noto Sans Khojki follows with a clear, large eye on every e and exits wide enough to pass light through, which is where the pair is strongest.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Hairline-free and shadow-free, Nippo has a crisp, technical look with small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Khudawadi counters with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook and little gap between capital and lowercase height.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kr: Noto Sans KR reads clean, with generous gaps in its curves and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height. Nippo cuts every stroke to one width, and the two sit together with a crisp, modern feel.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lao: Nippo brings wire-cut strokes and small letters standing almost as tall as capitals, with uninterrupted line width on every glyph. And Noto Sans Lao, with its x-height pushed well above the usual, makes the pair feel open and modern.
